problem:
Determine the number of pivot columns of the matrix $D,$ given by

$$
D=[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 0 & 0 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & -3 & 7 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 & 0 & -2 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

activity_context.topic_title: Identifying the Pivot Columns of a Matrix

examples.knowledge_point: Finding the Number of Pivot Columns of a Matrix
examples.problem:
Determine the number of pivot columns of the matrix $A,$ given by
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14072258/assets/eb0fc447f75650bb47da114b8cd4f0986b5f501333f61005e2c1f4989c3a11ed.png)
examples.worked_solution:
First, we need to convert $A$ to row echelon form:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 3 & 0 & -2 \\ 0 & -6 & 1 & 4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+2{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 3 & 0 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Looking at the row echelon form, we see that $A$ has $3$ pivots, and therefore the number of pivot columns is $3.$

feedback.problem:
The row echelon form matrix $B$ is given below. What are its **non**-pivot columns?

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}3 & -8 & 0 & 4 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & -1 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 7 & 8 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$
feedback.worked_solution:
Remember that the pivots of a matrix in row echelon form are the first non-zero entries in each row of the matrix.

We can see that $B$ has $3$ pivots in the $1$st, $3$rd, and $4$th columns:

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}3 & -8 & 0 & 4 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & -1 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 7 & 8 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$

Therefore, the only non-pivot columns are the $2$nd and $5$th columns.
